text: Recent visitor feedback shows several areas needing attention at the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library. Some guests found the interactive exhibits overly focused on AI, with a few saying the experience lacked substantive historical content and was not accessible for taller visitors. Lighting and signage were also criticized for making navigation difficult. There were complaints about the food quality and wait times. Additionally, timed entry procedures caused confusion, with some visitors unsure about arrival flexibility despite long lines at peak times.

While many appreciated the interactive elements and the building’s architecture, there were repeated mentions of crowding and parking issues. Overall, the average rating remains positive, but attention to exhibit design and visitor wayfinding could improve the experience.
